properties.areaDesc: West Polk; Norman; Kittson; Roseau; West Marshall; East Marshall; Pennington; Red Lake; East Polk; Pembina; Eastern Walsh County; Grand Forks; Traill
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 27 at 4:08AM CST by NWS Grand Forks ND
properties.description:
Light rain has started to push into northeastern North Dakota, and
will continue into the northern Red River Valley over the next
few hours. While the rain will be very light and many locations
will see temperatures rising above freezing as it moves in, a few
areas could see slippery roads develop early this morning as
light rain falls onto freezing ground. Motorists should slow down
to a safe speed and plan extra time to reach their destination.
Don't use cruise control. Be especially careful around stop
lights and intersections.

Check road conditions...
By Phone: call 511
Website for North Dakota: travel.dot.nd.gov
Website for Minnesota: 511mn.org

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Collier County
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 27 at 4:52AM EST until November 27 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Collier County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Statement, through Friday
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 1:31AM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft.

* WHERE...The Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday
morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

morning.

deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/rah/rivers.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 345 PM EST.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 27 at 3:31AM EST by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
Areas of light snow will continue across portions of far North
Georgia through around mid-morning. At elevations below 2500 feet,
little to no accumulation is expected, though a dusting may occur
on grassy and elevated surfaces. At elevations near or above 2500
feet, total accumulations up to 2 inches are possible.

Overall, travel impacts should be minimal, as recent warm
temperatures should keep most roadways clear. However, motorists
should exercise caution, particularly on bridges and overpasses
and along roadways at higher elevations where isolated slick spots
may develop. For more information or to report snowfall amounts
at your location, please visit www.weather.gov/atlanta.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
6-8 feet, sets up to 10 feet along west-facing beaches. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, surf of 4 to 6 feet with sets to 7 feed
and minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 1 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST early this
morning. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 1 PM PST this
afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides peak this morning around 7.5-7.7
feet MLLW. Surf will be falling this morning but remain elevated
into Saturday, especially for west-facing beaches. Sets up to 7
feet. Despite lower surf and waning tides, localized coastal
flooding is still likely through the Saturday morning high
tides.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Kent MD.

* WHEN...Until midnight EST tonight.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
bayside communities and along tidal waterways. Some roads
become impassable. Minor damage to vulnerable structures may
begin to occur.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 11:14PM PST until November 27 at 3:34PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 PM PST Thursday the stage was 17.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 PM PST Thursday was 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue to hover near a
crest of 17.8 feet through this evening. It will then fall below
flood stage tomorrow morning.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 615 AM PST.

properties.description:
We will continue to some light rain or snow in the lower
elevations with little or no snow accumulation overnight, but the
higher elevations especially above 2500 feet will be primarily
snow overnight into Friday morning. While the ground is warm, some
of the higher terrain of the Plateau, southwest Virginia, the
east Tennessee mountains, and the mountains of southwest North
Carolina will see around an inch of snow accumulation. A few
mountain peaks may see accumulations in the 2 to 3 inch range.

be alert for slippery spots on roadways if traveling in these
areas, especially on bridges and overpasses.

Please plan accordingly if planning to travel in or through these
areas.  Using extra caution is advised, slow down, and allow
extra distance between yourself and other vehicles.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 26 at 3:36PM HST until November 27 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES
OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI...AND NORTH FACING SHORES OF MAUI
AND THE BIG ISLAND...

.An extra-large north-northwest (330 to 350 degree) swell will
maintain warning level surf tonight and gradually subside through
Friday morning.

* WHAT...For north-facing shores, surf heights 20 to 30 ft
tonight, subsiding to 20 to 25 ft tomorrow morning. For west-
facing shores, surf 12 to 16 ft tonight, subsiding to 10 to 14
ft tomorrow morning.

* WHERE...Portions of Kauai, Maui, Molokai, Niihau, Oahu and the
Big Island.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful
currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make
navigating the channels dangerous.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 1:12PM AKST until November 28 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding with water levels 1.5 to 3.0 feet
above the highest tide line possible.

* WHERE...Kipnuk, Kongiganak, and Kwigillingok.

* WHEN...6 PM Today to 6 AM Saturday. Particularly the overnight
high tide tonight and Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Potential flooding of low lying areas, including
lowest portions of boardwalks. Coastal erosion possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long duration of onshore winds combined
with higher-than-normal tides will increase the potential for
elevated water levels, high surf, and coastal erosion tonight
and Friday night. Tides will remain higher than normal into the
middle of next week.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 6 AM AKST SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 26 at 1:04PM AKST until November 27 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations 3
to 6 inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 to 50 mph. Visibilities
reduced to one half mile or less due to blowing snow.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow could
significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest chances of blowing snow are on Nunivak
Island and along the Kuskokwim Delta Coast north of Kipnuk.
Southeast winds become westerly early Friday morning. The strongest
wind gusts are expected Friday morning after winds become westerly.
Conditions are expected to gradually improve late Friday afternoon
as snowfall tapers off and winds begin to decrease.
properties.instruction: Use caution while traveling.

NWSheadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 PM AKST FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: SW Kenai Peninsula
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 26 at 1:04PM AKST until November 27 at 8:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Breaking waves of 2 to 4 feet. West-southwest winds 15 to
20 mph gusting to 25 to 30 mph.

* WHERE...Homer Spit.

* WHEN...2 PM to 8 PM Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Water and light debris could wash over portions of the
Homer Spit Road. Minor beach erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Friday sees strong west to southwest winds,
which when combined with the high tide could produce minor
impacts along the Homer Spit. In addition, the King Tide is also
anticipated during Friday's afternoon's high tide cycle.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 11:59AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Periods of snow become increasingly likely through Thursday as a
front approaches the coast. Southeast winds gusting up to 35 mph
shift southerly and peak up to 40 mph late Friday. The
combination of falling snow and strong winds are expected to lead
to periods of reduced visibility due to blowing snow, with
visibilities falling to 1 mile or less at times. Total snow
accumulations of 1 to 3 inches expected through Friday night. The
heaviest snow is expected near Cape Romanzof including Chevak,
Hooper Bay, and Scammon Bay.

properties.areaDesc: St Lawrence Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 11:59AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:

winds gusting up to 45 mph. This will likely result in lowered
visibility to 1 mile or less at times. Temperatures will be
hovering near 32 degrees which means blowing snow will only be
expected when it is actively snowing. Total snow accumulations
around 2 to 4 inches expected through Friday evening.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 26 at 10:33AM AKST until November 27 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Periods of blizzard conditions. Winds gusting as high as 45
mph.

* WHERE...Point Thompson.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very little additional falling snow is
expected. Strong winds will blow snow already on the ground to
create areas of low visibility near the surface. No significant
visibility reductions are expected at Barter Island/Kaktovik due to
open water limiting the availability of blowable snow to the east.
properties.instruction:

vehicle in case of an emergency.

properties.areaDesc: Shishmaref; Bering Strait Coast; Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 26 at 10:28AM AKST until November 28 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations up
to two inches. Winds gusting up to 40 mph.

* WHERE...Bering Strait Coast, Interior Seward Peninsula, Diomede,
and Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...From 3 PM Friday to 9 AM AKST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel may be impacted. Blowing and falling snow could
reduce visibility to 1/2 mile or less at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow totals of 0.5 to 2 inches expected for
most locations. South facing slopes along the southern Seward
Peninsula including near Nome could see up to 3 inches of snow.
Winds peak overnight Friday into Saturday and rapidly weaken
through Saturday.
properties.instruction:

NWSheadline: WINTER WEATHER ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 3 PM FRIDAY TO 9 AM AKST SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Bell; Harlan
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 1:13PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Rain will mix with or changeover to wet snow as temperatures quickly
drop into the lower to mid 30s this evening. The snow may become
briefly heavy overnight, allowing for minor snow accumulations above
2,000-ft elevation. A brief period of slushy conditions is possible
on high-elevation road surfaces. Valley bottoms will likely see any
minor snow accumulations confined to grassy and elevated surfaces.

If traveling over higher elevations, especially overnight, you should
expect poor visibility with periods of wet snow and slushy road
surfaces.

Snow and rain will diminish in intensity Friday before gradually
ending.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

NWSheadline: MINOR SNOW ACCUMULATIONS POSSIBLE MAINLY ABOVE 2,000-FT ELEVATION TONIGHT INTO FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Essex; Southeast Middlesex; Suffolk; Eastern Norfolk; Eastern Plymouth; Barnstable; Dukes; Nantucket
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 12:54PM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (3.1 to 12.9 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...Eastern Essex MA, Southeast Middlesex MA, Suffolk MA,
Eastern Norfolk MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Barnstable MA, Dukes
MA and Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Shallow pockets of flooding less than one foot deep
affects the lowest lying areas along the coast, including
Morrissey Boulevard in Boston. Most roads remain passable.
Flooding up to one foot deep affects coastal roads on the
North Shore from Salem to Gloucester and Newburyport. Rough
surf will cause flooding on some coastal roads around the time
of high tide due to splashover. Roads remain passable. Low
lying areas and roads near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy
Street, may experience pockets of shallow flooding less than
one foot deep.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 8 AM TO 3 PM EST FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Southern Bristol; Southern Plymouth; Southeast Providence; Eastern Kent; Bristol; Washington; Newport
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 12:54PM EST until November 27 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half
foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways (4.7 to 7.1 feet
Mean Lower Low Water). For the second Coastal Flood Advisory,
up to one half foot of inundation above ground level expected
in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways (3.7 to
7.1 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...In Massachusetts, Southern Bristol MA and Southern
Plymouth MA Counties. In Rhode Island, Southeast Providence
RI, Eastern Kent RI, Bristol RI, Washington RI and Newport RI
Counties.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 PM this
evening to 1 AM EST Friday. For the second Coastal Flood
Advisory, from 7 AM to 1 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding occurs along the most
vulnerable shoreline locales in Newport, Portsmouth and
Middletown. This includes flooding at parking lots near
beaches in Newport, and a portion of Hazard Road. Minor
coastal flooding also occurs on several streets in the Common
Fence Point area.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 4:34AM PST until November 27 at 9:27AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near
record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift
flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including
SR 106, and much of the farm land.   Flooding will occur all along
the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It
will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises
through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage
possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1245 PM PST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FRIDAY MORNING

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:07PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 155 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow around 2500 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately downstream
of the dam also indicated a stage just above 8.5 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
